rationale: Complex multi-bar chart exposed as role=img with only a short aria-label 'Sales chart'. No aria-describedby, figcaption, details, adjacent data table, or longdesc carries the four data values, so the required long description is missing.
citation: SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A): 'All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose...' — for complex content an equivalent purpose requires more than a short label.

rationale: Complex revenue chart (placeholder img) whose short alt 'Quarterly revenue' omits all the data the chart presents; there is no adjacent table, figcaption, details, describedby, or longdesc, so no long description exists.
citation: Understanding 1.1.1 / G92: 'Providing long description for non-text content that serves the same purpose and presents the same information.'

rationale: A process flowchart SVG whose only text is a <title> naming it; the <title> is a short label and gives none of the steps or branches. No <desc>, describedby, or adjacent text equivalent provides the long description the flow requires.
citation: Trusted Tester 5.1 condition for 1.1.1 / complex images: charts, graphs and diagrams require a long description in addition to a short text alternative.

rationale: A market-share segment chart sits in a <figure>, but the <figcaption> is the generic label 'Figure 1.' rather than the data; the only candidate long-desc source is empty of equivalent content, so the long description is effectively missing.
citation: Failure F65 analogue: the text alternative is omitted or insufficient for the content's purpose; a generic caption does not serve the equivalent purpose of a complex image.

rationale: The chart declares aria-describedby='pop-desc' but no element with id 'pop-desc' exists, so the reference dangles and no long description resolves; the apparent source does not actually provide text.
citation: SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A): 'All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose...' — a dangling describedby provides no equivalent text.

rationale: A stacked energy chart has an adjacent <table>, but that table is an unrelated office-hours table, not the chart's data; an unrelated table is not an equivalent, so no long description for the chart exists.
citation: Understanding 1.1.1 / G92: 'Providing long description for non-text content that serves the same purpose and presents the same information.' — an unrelated table does not present the same information.

rationale: A map (placeholder img) conveying locations and spatial relationships has only the short alt 'Map of store locations'; no table, describedby, figcaption, details, or longdesc supplies the equivalent textual information, so the long description is missing.
citation: EN 301 549 clause 9.1.1.1 (maps to WCAG 1.1.1): non-text content requires a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose.

rationale: A multi-panel infographic (placeholder img) carrying statistics and steps has only a short alt 'Recycling infographic'; there is no figcaption, table, details, describedby, or longdesc, so none of its content is available as a long description.
citation: SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A): 'All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose...' — a label cannot convey an infographic's content.

rationale: A network architecture diagram (placeholder img) whose alt merely echoes the filename 'network-architecture-v2.png', conveying nothing about the topology; there is no long-desc source, so the required long description is absent.
citation: Failure F65 analogue: the text alternative is omitted or insufficient; a filename repeated as alt does not serve the equivalent purpose of a diagram.

rationale: A satisfaction-trend line chart has a <details><summary>Chart description</summary></details> that looks like a long-description container but has an empty body, so no equivalent text resolves and the long description is missing.
citation: Understanding 1.1.1 / G92: 'Providing long description for non-text content that serves the same purpose and presents the same information.' — an empty container presents no information.

rationale: aria-describedby='budget-desc' resolves to a real element, but that element contains no text, so the long description it is supposed to carry is empty; the source resolves structurally but provides no equivalent content.
citation: SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A): 'All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose...' — an empty describedby target provides no equivalent.

rationale: A minimal two-bar chart whose aria-label already states both values; no long-desc source is present (which a presence detector can see), but whether this image is 'complex enough' to REQUIRE a long description is a judgment, so the runner should abstain rather than decide.
citation: Trusted Tester 5.1 condition for 1.1.1 / complex images: charts, graphs and diagrams require a long description in addition to a short text alternative — applicability turns on whether the image is complex.

rationale: The complex bar chart declares aria-describedby='sales-desc', which resolves to a paragraph giving every quarter's value and the high/low; this is a resolvable long-description source presenting the same information.
citation: Understanding 1.1.1 / G92: 'Providing long description for non-text content that serves the same purpose and presents the same information.'

rationale: The placeholder chart image is immediately followed by a data <table> presenting the same monthly visitor values; the adjacent equivalent data table is a recognised long-description source.
citation: G73: 'Providing a long description in another location with a link to it that is immediately adjacent to the non-text content.' — here an immediately adjacent equivalent data table presents the same data.

rationale: The temperature line chart sits in a <figure> whose <figcaption> is a genuine multi-sentence long description carrying every month's value and the overall trend, serving the equivalent purpose.
citation: G74: 'Providing a long description in text near the non-text content, with a reference to the location of the long description in the short description.'

rationale: Below the Gantt timeline chart a <details><summary> exposes a full long description of all three phases and their week ranges; the details element is a resolvable long-description location.
citation: G73: 'Providing a long description in another location with a link to it that is immediately adjacent to the non-text content.'

rationale: aria-describedby='funnel-desc' resolves to a visually-hidden (clip) div that still contains the full equivalent text (stage counts and conversion rate) exposed to assistive technology; the long-description source resolves and is non-empty.
citation: SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A): 'All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose...' — a visually-hidden but programmatically-available description satisfies this.

rationale: The diagram image uses the legacy longdesc attribute pointing to a description resource, and additionally provides an in-page 'Long description' link to a section containing the full equivalent text, so a resolvable long-description source exists.
citation: H45 (longdesc): providing a long description for an image using the longdesc attribute; combined with G73 the in-page fallback gives an immediately reachable long description.

rationale: A visible 'Long description' link immediately after the data-flow diagram resolves to an in-page section that describes every stage and connection in text; this is a recognised adjacent long-description location.
citation: G73: 'Providing a long description in another location with a link to it that is immediately adjacent to the non-text content.'

rationale: The login flowchart SVG carries a short <title> for the name and a full <desc> describing every step, branch, and the lockout rule; assistive technology exposes the <desc> as the long description via aria-describedby.
citation: H53 (using the body of the object element) analogue for SVG: the in-content <desc> supplies the long description; G74 covers a long description in text near the non-text content.

rationale: The placeholder survey chart sits in a <figure> whose <figcaption> contains a correctly associated data table (scoped headers) presenting each response category and count; the figure carries an equivalent data table as the long description.
citation: Understanding 1.1.1 / G92: 'Providing long description for non-text content that serves the same purpose and presents the same information.'

rationale: aria-describedby='headcount-desc' resolves to a sibling region that lists the per-quarter headcount numbers and the strongest growth period; the describedby points to real descriptive text presenting the same data.
citation: Understanding 1.1.1 / G92: 'Providing long description for non-text content that serves the same purpose and presents the same information.'

rationale: A long-description source IS present (a <figcaption>) and it conveys the trend, but it omits the actual values; the presence signal is detectable, yet whether a partial description is an adequate EQUIVALENT is a judgment, so the runner should abstain.
citation: G74: 'Providing a long description in text near the non-text content, with a reference to the location of the long description in the short description.' — adequacy of a partial description is a judgment about equivalent purpose.
